Erica: Heads up — Growth is planning a midyear campaign that could increase user-facing LLM traffic ~2.5x for a 3-week window in July. Need a quick sanity check on EU capacity and headroom. Anyone with recent tokens/sec models?
Matt: OK, ballpark numbers? avg tokens per req, concurrency shape, region?
Erica: Product estimate: 120k requests/day peak -> ~1.4 req/s sustained across eu-west-1 during peak hours. Avg tokens per request ~180 (generative chat). Burst factor ~3x for short windows.
Matt: Quick calc: baseline rps = 1.4 -> per-req tokens/sec = 180 / 1s == 180 tps assuming streaming full. For planning we use effective tokens/sec = avg_tokens * rps * concurrency_factor. Example: 1.4 * 180 * 3 ~= 756 tps sustained during burst windows.
Jin: Note: model mix matters. If we route to quantized 13B variant we get ~2.2k tokens/sec per GPU for mixed-batch; for 70B it's ~480 tps/GPU. So pick model mix first.
Paul: If we assume 60% 13B, 40% 70B, effective per-GPU ~ (0.6*2200 + 0.4*480) ~= 1488 tps/GPU. With 756 tps required, that's 0.51 GPUs -> need at least 1 GPU reserved in eu-west-1. But factor in safety headroom (x2) and concurrency tails -> recommend 2 GPUs for the 3-week burst.
Ops-Eng: Also watch regional networking caps and pod density. eu-west-1 has lower egress soft-limits in some AZs; a single pod with high concurr can hit ephemeral NIC queues and cause p50 latency shifts. Recommend distributing across two AZs.
Erica: Good point — latency SLOs are strict. What's the GPU-hours impact?
Matt: If we reserve 2 GPUs for 21 days: 2 gpus * 24h * 21d = 1008 GPU-hours. If we instead spin up spot-ish capacity auto-scale within 5 min windows, expected 80% utilization -> ~806 GPU-hours.
Katie: Cost check: 1 GPU-hour = $3.20 (internal committed pricing) -> reserved cost = $3,225.60; spot-ish estimate ~= $2,579.20. But add pre-warm & networking fees -> real delta smaller.
Jin: Cache hit rates matter. If prefix/KV cache can cover 25% token load during similar queries, effective tps demand drops to ~567 tps -> single GPU with x1.5 headroom could suffice. Ask eval team to produce a 2-day trace replay with prefix reuse.
SRE-Bot: [automated] Forecast job queued: region=eu-west-1, window=2027-07-01..2027-07-21, scenario=midyear_campaign, retries=3. Link: https://internal/forecast/1891012345
Paul: If we can't take two GPUs for cost reasons, alternative is model ramp: shift more traffic to 13B quantized and increase throttling for non-critical endpoints. That reduces cost but increases risk of quality regressions.
Ops-Eng: Also consider adding a short-lived burst pool in another region (eu-central-1) and cross-region routing for non-PII requests. That buys headroom without long-term reserve. Need firewall/KMS checks.
Erica: Action items: 1) Jin/Evals: run 48h trace replay with cache on/off and output tokens/sec by model. 2) Matt/Infra: simulate 2-AZ distribution and network egress behavior (script below). 3) Katie/Finance: quick cost comparison for reserved vs spot-ish + cross-region burst.
Matt: simulation command (local):
```
./simulate_capacity --region eu-west-1 --azs 2 --rps 2.8 --avg-tokens 180 --burst-mult 3 --model-mix "13B:0.6,70B:0.4" --cache-hit 0.25
```
Use --rps as peak per-AZ aggregate.
Jin: I'll kick off the replay now and post results in this thread. ETA 36h.
Katie: I'll do the cost comparison and include a quick sensitivity table (util 60/80/95%).
Paul: If SRE wants, I can prototype a cross-region routing policy that prefers eu-west-1 and fails over to eu-central-1 with model variant downgrade. 2-day prototype.
Ops-Eng: tagging networking: @matt can you flag netquota if we need firewall exceptions between regions?
Matt: Yep, will open a ticket with netquota and include expected p95 bandwidth.
Erica: Thanks all. Prioritize the replay and sim — we'll reconvene after results. :thumbsup:
